question.problem:
Plot the graph $y=f(x+2)$ for $y=f(x)$ given below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14214993/assets/6ca96bba855899f9b87ae06c166503c9af739fcd6bb2ec466a73b75cc70dde7f.png)
question.worked_solution:
The graph of $y=f(x+2)$ is a horizontal translation of the graph of $y=f(x)$ by $2$ units to the *left*. So, every point on the graph of $y=f(x+2)$ is two units *to the left* of the corresponding point on the graph of $y=f(x).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14214993/assets/758899a1abd5298429059016a4127db61eda014e8c46e0539e9226c5641e5ceb.png)
